topics.label: Rain
facts: Rain is water falling from clouds in the sky.
Rain gives water to plants, animals, and rivers.
Rain happens when tiny drops of water in clouds join together and get heavy.
After rain, you can sometimes see a rainbow in the sky.

questions.fact: Rain is water that falls from clouds when the drops get heavy.

questions.q: What does rain give to plants?
questions.fact: Plants drink rainwater through their roots.
Rain falls from clouds in the sky.

questions.q: What can you sometimes see in the sky after rain?
questions.fact: Sunlight shining through rain drops makes a rainbow.

topics.label: Snow
facts: Snow is made of tiny ice crystals that fall from clouds.
Snow falls when the air is very cold.
Each snowflake has six sides, and no two snowflakes are exactly alike.
Snow covers the ground like a white blanket and can be used to build snowmen.

questions.fact: Snow is made of tiny ice crystals that form in cold clouds.

choices: When the air is very cold
questions.fact: Snow falls when the air is cold enough for water drops to freeze.

questions.q: How many sides does a snowflake have?
questions.fact: Snowflakes have six sides, and every one has its own shape.

questions.q: What can you build with snow?
questions.fact: Snow sticks together, so you can roll it into balls and build a snowman.

topics.label: Wind
facts: Wind is air that is moving.
Wind can blow leaves, clouds, and kites through the sky.
Strong wind can bend trees and make waves on the sea.
Wind turbines use wind to make electricity.

questions.fact: Wind is air moving from one place to another.

questions.q: What can the wind blow through the sky?
questions.fact: Wind can lift a kite and carry it through the sky.

questions.q: What do wind turbines use wind to make?
questions.fact: Wind turbines turn in the wind and make electricity.

questions.q: What can strong wind do to trees?
choices: Make them grow taller at once
questions.fact: Strong wind can bend trees and even break branches.

topics.label: Thunder and Lightning
facts: Lightning is a big spark of electricity that jumps between clouds or between a cloud and the ground.
Thunder is the loud sound that lightning makes when it heats the air around it very quickly.
You see lightning before you hear thunder because light travels faster than sound.
During a thunderstorm, the safest place to be is indoors, away from tall trees and water.

choices: A big spark of electricity in the sky
questions.fact: Lightning is a huge spark of electricity between clouds or to the ground.
Thunder is the sound of air heating and expanding quickly around lightning.

questions.q: Why do you see lightning before you hear thunder?
questions.fact: Light reaches your eyes almost instantly, while sound takes longer to travel.

questions.q: Where is the safest place during a thunderstorm?
questions.fact: Staying indoors keeps you safe from lightning during a storm.
